controls: Leave dispatch_f16_strided and the free function API unchanged so other call sites keep thread-safe semantics
Create the strided kernel member in the primitive constructor, which runs single-threaded before execute_forward, so multi-threaded parallel() execution only reads an immutable object
Gate the change under the same XBYAK_RISCV_V && XBYAK_RISCV_V == 1 preprocessor block as the current f16 path
Measure benchdnn_max_create_ms to confirm the one-time JIT creation cost moves to creation and does not regress steady-state
reasons: Moving construction from a function-local thread-safe static to a member changes the thread-safety mechanism; if execute_forward could run concurrently with construction, a data race on the kernel pointer could occur
The kernel object holds jit_ker_ (generated code buffer); any write to it after publication would corrupt the executable code
The scatter path is one of several f16 code paths; changing only the wrapper but not fixing the symmetric gather/affine/exp-sub-sum dispatch would leave residual guard overhead elsewhere

conditions.description: Benchmark softmax_f16_upstream runs single-threaded by default (benchdnn without explicit multi-thread) so no concurrent writer reaches the guard
jit_rvv_softmax_f16_scatter is called once per softmax block inside the rvv_softmax.cpp:315-325 loop over outer_size*inner_size blocks
The strided JIT kernel is constructed exactly once (guard byte is constant after first call)
XBYAK_RISCV_V is defined and the f16 case (data_type::f16, inner_size>1) is the measured path

actions.proposal: Hoist the strided JIT kernel construction and dispatch out of the per-block hot path. In rvv_softmax.cpp, mirror the existing affine_kernel_ member pattern: add a member (e.g., std::unique_ptr<jit_rvv_softmax_f16_strided_kernel_t> strided_kernel_) created once in the rvv_softmax_fwd_t constructor (single-threaded primitive creation), and in execute_forward call (*strided_kernel_)(&p) directly for the f16 gather/scatter instead of dispatch_f16_strided<false>(&p) / dispatch_f16_strided<true>(&p). This removes the per-block thread-safe-static guard sequence (lb guard; fence r,rw; zext.b; beqz; indirect call) that currently executes for every block; the kernel object is immutable after construction so no per-call synchronization is needed. Keep the jit_rvv_softmax_f16_gather/scatter free functions and dispatch_f16_strided helper intact for any other callers.

correctness_checks: Run benchdnn softmax f16 correctness (--mode correctness) covering shapes with inner_size>1 so the scatter path executes
Run the same test with ONEDNN_NTHR=2 and 4 to confirm the hoisted kernel is created before parallel execution and remains immutable
Confirm call_params_t layout offsets (F16_STRIDED_OFF) are unchanged and the kernel object is fully constructed before execute_forward uses it

Per-call instruction count of the wrapper drops (no per-block fence r,rw + guard byte load), lowering total instructions in perf stat
Any remaining samples concentrate in the JIT-emitted vle16/vsse16 strided loop body rather than in the wrapper's guard block
benchdnn_avg_ms for softmax_f16_upstream decreases; the dispatch wrapper no longer appears as the dominant sampled symbol

success_criteria: Samples in the guard-check block (c73a3c) of the scatter wrapper drop to near zero in a re-run perf annotate
softmax_f16_upstream benchdnn_avg_ms decreases relative to the 0.473820 ms baseline
softmax f16 correctness passes single- and multi-threaded (ONEDNN_NTHR=1,2,4) with identical results
Total instructions (perf stat instruction counter, 9,489,442,014 baseline) decreases by more than the guard-block share for the same workload

alternative_explanations.explanation: Sampling skid on the out-of-order C920v2 (metadata) could misplace cycles from the JIT kernel body or the jalr onto the immediately-following guard-check zext.b; without precise_ip data (baseline_gap: sampling IP precision) the single-instruction 97.9% share may overstate the guard block's true cost.

The JIT scatter kernel body is out-of-line and not covered by this annotate; if most cycles actually execute inside that JIT loop (vle16/vsse16 with stride mul), the wrapper guard block would be a smaller share of the total workload than the annotate suggests. The annotate only samples this wrapper symbol.

Branch-miss rate is 0.184% and IPC is 0.80, so the beqz guard branch is not mispredicting and the function is not compute-saturated; these counters are consistent with a dispatch/sync-dominated path rather than a stalled branch or FMA-bound loop.

findings.conclusion: jit_rvv_softmax_f16_scatter spends the dominant within-function sample share (97.9%) in the thread-safe static-local guard check of dispatch_f16_strided<false>() — including a per-call fence r,rw — which is redundant synchronization in the uncontended benchmark context, executed once per softmax block via rvv_softmax.cpp:321.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Wrapper ends with jalr to the JIT kernel followed by the stack-canary epilogue (ld a4,-40(s0); ld a5,0(s1); xor a5,a5,a4; bnez) and ret, so no tail jump is possible; no RAS-pressure or wrapper-frame evidence exists.

The 97.9% hotspot is in the host wrapper's guard-check block, not in JIT-emitted code; the JIT scatter body (vle16/vsse16 loop) is out-of-line and unsampled in this annotate, so no emitter-quality signal is observable.

Opposite direction: that pattern lowers a needed atomic helper to AMO/LR/SC under real contention; here there is provably no concurrent writer, so synchronization itself is redundant and should be eliminated, not hardened.
The specialized JIT RVV kernel is correctly selected and reached via the guard + jalr path; no generic/fallback path is entered, so no registration/dispatch repair applies.

findings.reasoning: 140/143 samples (97.9%) concentrate at c73a3c in the thread-safe-static guard block (lb a5,0(a5); fence r,rw; zext.b a5,a5; beqz) of dispatch_f16_strided<false>(). Source (jit_rvv_softmax_kernel.cpp:55-60, 171-177) shows jit_rvv_softmax_f16_scatter builds a call_params_t and calls dispatch_f16_strided<false>(&p), which constructs a function-local static kernel (thread-safe guard + fence) and then indirectly calls it via operator(). rvv_softmax.cpp:321 calls the scatter once per softmax block inside a loop over outer_size*inner_size blocks, so the guard+decorated-fence sequence executes once per block per execution. The JIT kernel is constructed exactly once (guard byte constant afterward), and benchdnn softmax_f16_upstream is a single-threaded benchmark, so no concurrent writer exists; the per-call fence r,rw and guard check are redundant synchronization in an uncontended context. Pattern profile signal 'fence in a provably nonconcurrent path' and mechanism 'fence drains the pipeline / high frequency magnifies small costs' match the observed hotspot and the 0.80 IPC / 0.184% branch-miss counters.
